G1100.def:
γλῶσσα, -ης, ἡ, 
[in LXX chiefly for לָשׁוֹן ;] 
__1. the tongue, as the organ of speech: Marc 7:33, 35 Luc 1:64 16:24, Actes 2:26" (LXX), Romains 3:13 (LXX) 14:11 (LXX), 1 Corinthiens 14:9, Philippiens 2:11, Jacques 1:26 3:5, 6 8, 1 Pierre 3:10" (LXX), 1Jo.3:18, Apocalypse 16:10; of a tongue-like object, Actes 2:3. 
__2. a tongue, language: Actes 2:11; joined with φυλή, λαός, ἔθνος, frequently in pl., Apocalypse 5:9 7:9 10:11 11:9 13:7 14:6 17:15; λαλεῖν ἑτέραις γ., Actes 2:4; γ. λαλεῖν καιναῖς, WH, txt. (RV, mg., omit καιναῖς), Marc 16:17; λαλεῖν γλώσσαις, γλώσσῃ (see ICC, ll. with; DB, iv, 793ff.), Marc 16:17, WH, txt., R, mg., Actes 10:46 19:6, 1 Corinthiens 12:30 13:1 14:2, 4-6, 13, 18, 23, 27, 39; γλῶσσαι (= λόγοι ἐν γλώσσῃ, 1 Corinthiens 14:19), 1 Corinthiens 13:8 14:22; γένη γλωσσῶν, 1 Corinthiens 12:10, 28; προσεύχεσθαι γλώσσῃ, 1 Corinthiens 14:14; γλῶσσαν ἔχειν, 1 Corinthiens 14:26 (Cremer, 163, 679).
†

G1101.def:
γλωσσόκομον, -ου, τό, vernac. form of cl. γλωσσοκομεῖον 
(γλῶσσα, κομέω), [in LXX for אָרוֹן, 2 Rois 6:11, 2 Chroniques 24:8, 10 11 * ;] 
__1. = cl. -εῖον (see supr.), a case for holding the reeds or tongues of musical instruments. 
__2. As in LXX, π. (MM, see word), a box, chest: Jean 12:6 13:29.
†

G1102.def:
γναφεύς, -έως, ὁ, Ion. and κοινή form of Att. κναφεύς 
(κνάπτω, to card wool), [in LXX for כָּבַס, 4Ki.18:17, Ésaïe 7:3 36:2 * ;] 
a fuller, cloth-dresser: Marc 9:3.†

G1103.def:
γνήσιος, -α, -ον 
(γίγνομαι), [in LXX: Sir.7:18, 3Ma.3:19 * ;] 
__1. prop., lawfully begotten, born in wedlock (in π., γυνὴ γ., a lawful wife; MM, see word). 
__2. true, genuine, sincere: Philippiens 4:3, 1 Timothée 1:2, Tite 1:4; as subst., τὸ γ. = ἡ γνησιότης, sincerity, 2 Corinthiens 8:8.
†

G1104.def:
γνησίως, adv., 
[in LXX: 2Ma.14:8, 3Ma.3:23 * ;] 
sincerely, honourably: Phi 2:20 (for a parallel in π., see MM, see word).†

G1105.def:
γνόφος (later form of δν-), 
[in LXX for אָפֵל, עֲרָפֶל, etc. ;] 
darkness, gloom (including "an element of tempest," Tr., Syn., §with): Hébreux 12:18.†
SYN.: ἀχλύς, ζόφος, σκότος (Tr., l.with; DB, i, 457a).

G1107.def:
γνωρίζω 
(γιγνώσκω), [in LXX chiefly for ידע hi. ;] 
__1. as most commonly in cl., to come to know, discover, know: Philippiens 1:22 (but cf. R, mg.). 
__2. to make known: with accusative, Romains 9:22, 23; with accusative of thing(s) da.t. of person(s), Luc 2:15, Jean 15:15 17:26, Actes 2:28" (LXX), 1 Corinthiens 15:1, 2 Corinthiens 8:1, Galates 1:11, Éphésiens 1:9 6:19, 21 Colossiens 4:7, 9 2 Pierre 1:16; with dative, before ὅτι, 1 Corinthiens 12:3; before τί, Colossiens 1:27; περί, Luc 2:17. Pass., Actes 7:13, Romains 16:26, Éphésiens 3:3, 6 10, Philippiens 4:6 (Cremer, 677; cf. ἀνα-, δια-γνωρίζω).
†

G1108.def:
γνῶσις, -εως, ἡ 
(γιγνώσκω), [in LXX chiefly for דַּעַת ;] 
__1. a seeking to know, inquiry, investigation. 
__2. knowledge, in NT, specially of the kn. of spiritual truth: absol., Luc 11:52, Romains 2:20 15:14, 1 Corinthiens 1:5 (Lft., Notes, 147) 8:1, 7, 10, 11, 13:2, 8 14:6, 2 Corinthiens 6:6 8:7 11:6, Éphésiens 3:19, Colossiens 2:3, 1 Pierre 3:7, 2 Pierre 1:5, 6; with genitive obj., σωτηρίας, Luc 1:77; τ. δόξης τ. θεοῦ, 2 Corinthiens 4:6; τ. θεοῦ, 2 Corinthiens 2:14 10:5; Χριστοῦ Ἰησοῦ, Philippiens 3:8 (see Deiss., LAE, 383.8), 2 Pierre 3:18; with genitive subjc., θεοῦ, Romains 11:33; λόγος γνώσεως, 1 Corinthiens 12:8; ψευδωνύμου γνώσεως, 1 Timothée 6:20.
† SYN.: σοφία, φρόνησις (cf. ἐπί-γνωσις and see Lft. on Colossiens 2:3; Cremer, 156).

G1109.def:
γνώστης, -ου, ὁ 
(γιγνώσκω), [in LXX chiefly for יִדְּעֹנִי ;] 
one who knows, an expert: Actes 26:3.†

G1110.def:
γνωστός, -ή, -όν, later form of γνωστός 
(γιγνώσκω), [in LXX for various parts of ידע ;] 
known: Actes 9:42; with dative, Jean 18:15, 16 (Rec.), Actes 1:19 2:14 4:10 13:38 15:18 19:17 28:22, 28; γ. σημεῖον, a notable (EV) sign, one that is matter of knowledge, Actes 4:16; γνωστὸν, Actes 15:17, 18; τὸ γνωστὸν θεοῦ, Romains 1:19; in pl., as subst., γνωστοί, acquaintances, Luc 2:44 23:49; so in sing., Jean 18:16 (WH).†

G1111.def:
γογγύζω, 
[in LXX chiefly for לוּן ;] 
to mutter, murmur: 1 Corinthiens 10:10; before κατά, Matthieu 20:11; πρός, Luc 5:30; περί, Jean 6:41, 61; μετ᾽ ἀλλήλων, Jean 6:43; with accusative, before περί, Jean 7:32 (cf. δια-γογγύζω).†

G1112.def:
γογγυσμός, -οῦ, ὁ, 
[in LXX: Ésaïe 58:9 (אָוֶן), Exode 16:7-9, Nombres 17:5, 10 (תְּלוּנָה), Wis.1:10, 11 Sir.46:7 * ;] 
a murmuring, muttering: Jean 7:12, Actes 6:1; ἄνευ γ., 1 Pierre 4:9; pl., χωρὶς γ., Philippiens 2:14.†

G1113.def:
γογγυστής, -οῦ, ὁ (γογγύζω); [in Sm.: Proverbes 26:22, Ésaïe 29:24; Th.: Proverbes 26:20 * ;] 
a murmurer: Ju 16.†

G1114.def:
γόης, -ητος, ὁ (γοάω, to wail), 
__1. a wailer. 
__2. a wizard. 
__3. an impostor (cf. γοητεία, trickery, 2Ma.12:24): 2 Timothée 3:13.
†

G1115.def:
Γολγοθά (Rec. -θᾶ; WH, mg., Γολγόθ, Jo, l.with, Aram. גָּלְגָּלְתָּא = Heb. גֻּלְגֹּלֶת, LXX, κρανίον, Juges 9:53, 2 Rois 9:35); indecl. (exc. Marc 15:22, -άν), 
Golgotha, the place of the crucifixion: Matthieu 27:33, Marc 15:22, Jean 19:17.†

G1116.def:
Γόμορρα, -ας, ἡ, and -ων, τά (Heb. עֲמֹרָה), 
Gomorrah, one of the cities of the plain (Gen.19): Matthieu 10:15, Romains 9:29" (LXX), 2 Pierre 2:6, Ju 7.†

G1117.def:
γόμος, -ου, ὁ 
(γέμω), [in LXX: Exode 23:5, 4Ki.5:17 (מַשָּׂא) * ;] 
a ship's freight, cargo: Actes 21:3, Apocalypse 18:11, 12.†

G1118.def:
γονεύς, -έως, ὁ 
(γίγνομαι), [in LXX for אָב, אֵם ;] 
a begetter, a father; mostly in pl., οἱ γ., parents: Luc 2:41, 43 8:56 21:16, Jean 9:2, 3 20, 22, 23 Romains 1:30, 2 Corinthiens 12:14, Éphésiens 6:1, Colossiens 3:20, 2 Timothée 3:2; accusative pl. (Hellenistic, see Thackeray, Gr., i, 148), γονεῖς, Matthieu 10:21, Marc 13:22, Luc 2:27 18:29, Jean 9:18.†

G1119.def:
γόνυ, -ατος, τό, 
[in LXX chiefly for בֶּרֶךְ ;] 
the knee: Hébreux 12:12; of a suppliant, προσπίπτειν τοῖς γ., Luc 5:8; so also τιθέναι τὰ γ., to kneel: Luc 22:41, Actes 7:60 9:40 20:36 21:5; in mockery, Marc 15:19; κάμπτειν τὰ γ., to bend the knee: Romains 11:4 (LXX) 14:11 (LXX), Éphésiens 3:14, Philippiens 2:10.†

G1120.def:
γονυπετέω, -ῶ) (γόνυ, πίπτω); 
__1. to fall on the knees: before ἔμπροσθεν, Matthieu 27:29. 
__2. to fall down before one: with accusative, Matthieu 17:14, Marc 1:40, R, txt., 10:17.
†

G1122.def:
γραμματεύς, -έως (accusative pl., -εῖς, see Bl., §8, 2), ὁ 
(γράμμα), [in LXX always for שׁטר in Hex., elsewhere chiefly for ספר ;] 
__1. a secretary; γ. τ. πόλεως, a state-clerk: Actes 19:35. 
__2. In π., of a military officer (Deiss., BS, 110f.). So Juges 5:14, 4Ki.25:19 (ספר), al. 
__3. a scribe, a biblical scholar, teacher of the law (so first in I Esther 8:3, II Esther 7:6; in Luc 5:17, νομοδιδάσκαλος; in Luc 10:25, νομικός): Matthieu 7:29, Marc 1:22, and frequently in Gosp. γ. καὶ ἀρχιερεῖς, Matthieu 2:4, and al.; γ. κ. Φαρισαῖοι, Matthieu 5:20, and al.; γ. μαθητευθεὶς τῇ βασιλείᾳ τ. οὐρ., Matthieu 13:52; ποῦ σοφός; ποῦ γ., 1 Corinthiens 1:20 (Cremer, 167; DB, iv, 420, 800).

G1123.def:
γραπτός, -ή, -όν 
(γράφω), [in LXX for מִכְתָּב ;] 
__1. painted. 
__2. written: Romains 2:15.
†

G1124.def:
γραφή, -ῆς, ἡ 
(γράφω), [in LXX chiefly for כְּתָב ;] 
__1. a drawing, painting. 
__2. 
__(a) writing; 
__(b) that which is written, a writing: πᾶσα γ., 2 Timothée 3:16; γ. ἅγιαι, Romains 1:2; προφητικαί, Romains 16:26; al αἱ γ. τ. προφητῶν, Matthieu 26:56; ἡ γ., αἱ γ., the sacred writings, the Scriptures (i.e. the OT; see Milligan, NTD, 205); in pl., when the sacred writings as a whole are meant, e.g. Matthieu 21:42 26:54, Jean 5:39, Romains 15:4; in sing., when a particular passage is referred to, as in Luc 4:21, Jean 19:24, Romains 4:3 9:17 10:11 11:2, Jacques 2:23 (Cremer, 165; DCG, ii, 584).

G1126.def:
γραώδης, -ες (γραῦς, an old woman, εἶδος), 
anile, old-womanish: 1 Timothée 4:7.†

G1127.def:
γρηγορέω, -ῶ, = Attic ἐργήγορα, pf. of ἐγείρω, which see, 
[in LXX (later bks. only) chiefly for שׁקד ;] 
__1. to be awake; metaphorically, of being alive, 1 Thessaloniciens 5:10. 
__2. to watch: Matthieu 24:43 26:38, 40 Marc 13:34 14:34, 37 Luc 12:37, 39; metaphorically, Matthieu 24:42 25:13 26:41, Marc 13:35, 37 14:38, Actes 20:31, 1 Corinthiens 16:13, 1 Thessaloniciens 5:6, 1 Pierre 5:8, Apocalypse 3:2, 3 16:15; before ἐν, Colossiens 4:2. (Cf. δια-γρηγορέω).†
SYN.: see: ἀγρθπνέω.

G1128.def:
γυμνάζω 
(γυμνός), [in LXX: 2Ma.10:15 * ;] 
__1. properly, to exercise naked. 
__2. Generally, to exercise, train the body or mind: 1 Timothée 4:7, Hébreux 5:14 12:11, 2 Pierre 2:14.
†

G1130.def:
γυμνιτεύω (Rec. γυμνητ-, V. Tdf ., Pr., 81), 
to be naked or scantily clad: 1 Corinthiens 4:11 (cf. ἐν ψύχει κ. γυμνότητι), 2 Corinthiens 11:27; γυμνοί, Jacques 2:15. In κοινή writers, γ. also means to go light-armed.†

G1131.def:
γυμνός, -ή, -όν, 
[in LXX chiefly for עָרוֹם ;] 
naked, without clothing, and sometimes (as frequently in cl.) scantily or poorly clad (Ésaïe 20:2ff., Tob.1:16, 2Ma.11:12): Matthieu 25:36, 38 43, 44, Marc 14:52, Jean 21:7, Actes 19:16, Jacques 2:15, Apocalypse 3:17 16:15, 17:16; as subst., to γ., the naked body, Marc 14:51. Metaphorical, of things exposed, Hébreux 4:13; of the soul without a body (Plat., Crat., with, 20, and cf. Deiss., LAE, 293), 2 Corinthiens 5:3; of seed, bare, 1 Corinthiens 15:37 (Cremer, 168).†

G1132.def:
γυμνότης, -ητος, ἡ 
(γυμνός), [in LXX for עֵירֹם, Deutéronome 28:48 * ;] 
nakedness: Romains 8:35, 2 Corinthiens 11:27, Apocalypse 3:18.†

G1133.def:
γυναικάριον, -ου, τό (diminutive of γυνή), 
a little woman; contemptuously, a silly woman (EV): 2 Timothée 3:6.†

G1134.def:
γυναικεῖος, -α, -ον 
(γυνή), [in LXX chiefly for אִשָּׁה ;] 
female: 1 Pierre 3:7.†

G1135G.def:
γυνή, -αικός, ἡ, 
[in LXX for אִשָּׁה ;] 
__1. a woman, married or unmarried: Matthieu 11:11 14:21, al.; ὕπανδρος γ., Romains 7:2; γ. χήρα, Luc 4:26; in vocat., γύναι implies neither reproof nor severity, but is used frequently as a term of respect and endearment, Matthieu 15:28, Jean 2:4, 4:21 19:26. 
__2. a wife: Matthieu 1:20, 1 Corinthiens 7:3, 4 al.; γ. ἀπολύειν, Marc 10:2, al.; γ. ἔχειν Marc 6:18; γ. λαβεῖν, Marc 12:19; γ. γαμεῖν, Luc 14:20. 
__3. a deaconess, 1 Timothée 3:11 (CGT, in l.).

G1135H.def:
γυνή, -αικός, ἡ, 
[in LXX for אִשָּׁה ;] 
__1. a woman, married or unmarried: Matthieu 11:11 14:21, al.; ὕπανδρος γ., Romains 7:2; γ. χήρα, Luc 4:26; in vocat., γύναι implies neither reproof nor severity, but is used frequently as a term of respect and endearment, Matthieu 15:28, Jean 2:4, 4:21 19:26. 
__2. a wife: Matthieu 1:20, 1 Corinthiens 7:3, 4 al.; γ. ἀπολύειν, Marc 10:2, al.; γ. ἔχειν Marc 6:18; γ. λαβεῖν, Marc 12:19; γ. γαμεῖν, Luc 14:20. 
__3. a deaconess, 1 Timothée 3:11 (CGT, in l.).

G1136.def:
Γώγ, ὁ (Heb. גּוֹג), indecl., 
Gog, assoc. with Magog (q.v): Apocalypse 20:8.†

G1137.def:
γωνία, -ας, ἡ 
(γόνυ), [in LXX chiefly for פִּנָּה ;] 
an angle, a corner: Matthieu 6:5, Actes 26:26; τ. τέσσαρας γ. τ. γῆς, Apocalypse 7:1, 20:8; κεφαλὴ γνωνίας (רֹאשׁ פִּנָּה, Ps 117(118):22, LXX), Matthieu 21:42, Marc 12:10, Luc 20:17, Actes 4:11, 1 Pierre 2:7.†

G1138.def:
Δαυείδ (Rec. Δαβίδ), ὁ, indecl. (Heb. דָּוִד), 
David, King of Israel: Matthieu 1:6; 12:3, and al.; σκηνὴ Δ., Actes 15:16; κλεὶς Δ., Apocalypse 3:7; θρόνος Δ., Luc 1:32; ῥίζα Δ., Apocalypse 5:5; βασιλεία Δ., Marc 11:10; υἱὸς Δ., the Messiah (Ps. Sol., 17:23; for other reff. in Jewish lit., see Dalman, Words, 317), Matthieu 1:1 9:27, and al.; ἐν Δ., i.e. the Psalter, Hébreux 4:7

G1139.def:
δαιμονίζομαι
(in cl. also δαιμονάω; δαίμων), [in Aq.: Ps 90(91):6 * ;] 
to be under the power of a δαίμων (δαιμόνιον, which see), to be possessed: Matthieu 15:22; elsewhere always ptcp., -ιζόμενος, -ισθείς: Matthieu 4:24; 8:16, 28, 33 9:32 12:22, Marc 1:32 15 16 18, Luc 8:36, Jean 10:21 (Cremer, 171).†

G1141.def:
δαιμονιώδης, -ες
(δαιμόνιον, εἶδος), [in Sm.: Ps 90(91):6 * ;] 
demon-like: Jacques 3:15 (Cremer, 171).†

G1142.def:
δαίμων, -ονος, ὁ, ἡ 
[in LXX for גַּד, Ésaïe 65:11 (א; δαιμονίῳ, AB) * ;] 
in cl. and NT = δαιμόνιον; a demon: Matthieu 8:31.†

G1143.def:
δάκνω 
[in LXX for נשׁךְ, Genèse 49:17, al., exc. Deutéronome 8:15 (שׂרף) ;] 
to bite: metaphorically, Galates 5:15.†

G1144.def:
δάκρυον (poët. form δάκρυ), -ου, τό, 
[in LXX for דִּמְעָה ;] 
a tear: Marc 9:24 (WH, txt., R, txt. omit), Actes 20:19, 31, 2 Corinthiens 2:4, 2 Timothée 1:4, Hébreux 5:7 12:17, Apocalypse 7:17 21:4; metaphorically, dative pl., δάκρυσι (La 2:11, Thuc., vii, 75; Bl., § 9, 3), Luc 7:38, 44.†

G1145.def:
δακρύω 
[in LXX for בָּכָה, etc. ;] 
to weep, shed tears: Jean 11:35.†
SYN.: κλαίω, of audible weeping, to cry; ὀδύρομαι, of grief expressed verbally, to lament; θρηνέω, of formal lamentation, to sing a dirge; ἀλαλάζω, to wail in Oriental fashion; στενάζω, of grief expressed by inarticulate sounds, to groan.

G1146.def:
δακτύλιος, -ου, ὁ
(δάκτυλος), [in LXX chiefly for טַבַּעַת ;] 
a ring: Luc 15:22.†

G1147.def:
δάκτυλος, -ου, ὁ 
[in LXX chiefly for אֶצְבַּע ;] 
a finger: Matthieu 23:4, Marc 7:33, Luc 11:46 16:24, Jean 8:6, 8 20:25, 27; metaphorically, δ. θεοῦ (cf. Exode 8:19), Luc 11:20.†

G1148.def:
Δαλμανουθά, ἡ
indecl., 
Dalmanutha, an unidentified place near the Sea of Galilee: Marc 8:10 (cf. Μαγαδάν).†

G1149.def:
Δαλματία (L, Δελ-), -ας, ἡ 
Dalmatia, a part of Illyria on E. coast of the Adriatic: 2 Timothée 4:10.†

G1150.def:
δαμάζω 
[in LXX: Daniel 2:40 (חֲשַׁל) * ;] 
to tame, subdue: Marc 5:4, Jacques 3:7; metaphorically, τ. γλῶσσαν, Jacques 3:8 (Field, Notes, 237f.).†

G1151.def:
δάμαλις, -εως, ἡ
(fem. of δαμάλης, a bullock), [in LXX chiefly for פָּרָה, עֶגְלָה ;] 
a heifer, Hébreux 9:13.†

G1152.def:
Δάμαρις, -ιδος, ἡ
(δάμαρ, poët., a wife), 
Damaris: Actes 17:34.†

G1154.def:
Δαμασκός, -οῦ, ἡ (Heb. דַּמֶּשֶׂק), 
Damascus: Actes 9:2ff. 22:5ff.26.12,20, 2 Corinthiens 11:32, Galates 1:17.†

G1155.def:
δανίζω
(late form of cl. -είζω, Rec., Bl., § 3; Thackeray, Gr., 85f.) [in LXX chiefly for לוה (Proverbes 19:17) ;] 
to lend money on interest: Luc 6:34, 35; mid., to borrow: Matthieu 5:42.†
SYN.: κίχρημι (see: χράω), to lend in a friendly way.

G1156.def:
δάνιον, -ου, τό 
(late form of δάνειον, Rec.; see: δανίζω), [in LXX: Deutéronome 24:11 (נָשָׁה) 15:8, 10 (עָבַט hi.), 4Ma.2:8 * ;] 
a loan: Matthieu 18:27.†

G1157.def:
δανιστής, -οῦ, ὁ 
(late form of -ειστής, Rec.; see: δανείζω), [in LXX: 4Ki.4:1, Psa.108(109):11 (נשׁה), Proverbes 29:13 (רָשׁ), Sir.29:28 * ;] 
a money-lender: Luc 7:41.†

G1158.def:
Δανιήλ, ὁ, indecl. (Heb. דָּנִיֵּאל, God is my Judge), 
Daniel, the prophet: Matthieu 24:15.†

G1159.def:
δαπανάω, -ῶ 
[in LXX: Tob.1:7, 1Ma.14:32, al. ;] 
__1. to spend, expend: with accusative, Marc 5:26; before ἐπί, with dative of person(s), Actes 21:24; ὑπέρ, 2 Corinthiens 12:15. 
__2. to consume, squander: Luc 15:14; ἐν τ. ἡδσναῖς (on the constr. with ἐν, see Hort, Mayor, in l.), Jacques 4:3 (cf. ἐκ-, προσ- δ.).†

G1160.def:
δαπάνη, -ης, ἡ 
[in LXX: Esther 6:4, 8 (נִפְקָא), Dan LXX Bel 1:21, al. ;] 
expense, cost: Luc 14:28.†

G1161.def:
δέ (before vowels δ᾽; on the general neglect of the elision in NT, see WH, App., 146; Tdf., Pr., 96), 
post-positive conjunctive particle; 
__1. copulative, but, in the next place, and, now (Abbott, JG, 104): Matthieu 1:2ff., 2 Corinthiens 6:15, 16, 2 Pierre 1:5-7; in repetition for emphasis, Romains 3:21, 22, 9:30, 1 Corinthiens 2:6, Galates 2:2, Philippiens 2:8; in transition to something new, Matthieu 1:18, 2:19, Luc 13:1, Jean 7:14, Actes 6:1, Romains 8:28, 1 Corinthiens 7:1 8:1, al.; in explanatory parenthesis or addition, Jean 3:19, Romains 5:8, 1 Corinthiens 1:12, Éphésiens 2:4, 5:32, al.; ὡς δέ, Jean 2:9; καὶ . . . δέ, but also, Matthieu 10:18, Luc 1:76, Jean 6:51, Romains 11:23, al.; καὶ ἐὰν δέ, yea even if, Jean 8:16. 
__2. Adversative, but, on the other hand, prop., answering to a foregoing μέν (which see), and distinguishing a word or clause from one preceding (in NT most frequently without μέν; Bl., §77, 12): ἐὰν δέ, Matthieu 6:14, 23, al.; ἐγὼ (σὺ, etc.) δέ, Matthieu 5:22, 6:6, Marc 8:29, al.; ὁ δέ, αὐτὸς δέ, Marc 1:45, Luc 4:40, al.; after a negation, Matthieu 6:19, 20, Romains 3:4, 1 Thessaloniciens 5:21, al.

G1162.def:
δέησις, -εως, ἡ
(δέομαι), [in LXX for תְּחִנָּה, רִנָּה, תְּפִלָּה, etc. ;] 
__1. a wanting, need (so Ps 21(22):25). 
__2. an asking, entreaty, supplica­tion; in NT always addressed to God: Luc 1:13, 2 Corinthiens 1:11, Philippiens 1:19, 2 Timothée 1:3, Jacques 5:16, 1 Pierre 3:12" (LXX) ; with νηστεῖαι, Luc 2:37; προσυνχή, -αί, Éphésiens 6:18, Philippiens 4:6, 1 Timothée 2:1 5:5; ἱκετηρίαι, Hébreux 5:7; προσκαρτέρησις, Éphésiens 6:18; ἐντεύξεις, 1 Timothée 2:1; δ. ποιεῖσθαι (Deiss., BS, 250), Luc 5:33, Philippiens 1:4 (pl.), 1 Timothée 2:1; before ὑπέρ, 2 Corinthiens 9:14, Philippiens 1:4; περί, Éphésiens 6:18; πρός, Romains 10:1.†
SYN.: προσευχή, used of prayer in general, while δ. gives prominence to the sense of need; on the other hand, δ. is used as well of requests from man to man, while π. is limited to prayer to God. ἔντευξις, in the π., is the regular word for petition to a superior (Deiss., BS, 250; cf. the Pauline ἐντυγχάνειν, to entreat). Cf. also εὐχή. (Jacques 5:15), αἴτημα, ἱκετηρία (Tr., Syn., § li; Cremer, 73, 174, 684).

G1163.def:
δεῖ impersonal (δέω), 
[in LXX chiefly for infin. with לְ ;] 
one must, it is necessary: with inf., Matthieu 26:54, Marc 13:7, Actes 5:29, al.; with accusative and inf., Matthieu 16:21, Marc 8:31, Jean 3:7, Actes 25:10, al.; with ellipse of accusative, Matthieu 23:23; of accusative, and inf., Marc 13:14, Romains 1:27 8:26; οὐ (μὴ) δεῖ (non licet), ought not, must not: Actes 25:24, 2 Timothée 2:24; impf., ἔδει, of necessity or obligation in past time regarding a past event (Bl., § 63, 4), Matthieu 18:33, Luc 15:32, Jean 4:4, Actes 27:21, al.; periphr., δέον ἐστίν (as in Attic, χρεών ἐστι = χρή, see: δέον), Actes 19:36; id., with ellipse of ἐστίν, 1 Pierre 1:6 τὰ μὴ δέοντα (= ἃ οὐ δεῖ 1 Timothée 5:13.
SYN.: ὀφείλει, expressing moral obligation, as distinct from δεῖ, denoting logical necessity and χρή, a need which results from the fitness of things (see Tr., Syn., § cvii, 10; Westc. on Hébreux 2:1, 1 Jean 2:6; Hort on Jacques 3:10).

G1164.def:
δεῖγμα, -τος, τό 
(δείκνυμι); 
__1. (cl.) a thing shown, a specimen. 
__2. = cl. παράδ- (cf. ὑπόδ-, 2 Pierre 2:6), an example (a warning): Ju 7.†

G1165.def:
δειγματίζω 
(δεῖγμα), 
a rare word (ICC, ll. with), to make a show of, to expose: Matthieu 1:19 (Rec. παραδ-, which see), Colossiens 2:15.†

G1167.def:
δειλία, -ας, ἡ 
(δειλός), [in LXX for אֵימָה, מְחִתָּה, etc. ;] 
cowardice, timidity (never in good sense): 2 Timothée 1:7.†
SYN.: φόβος, fear, in general, good or bad; εὐλάβεια (which see), apprehension generally, but chiefly pious fear, "that careful and watchful reverence which pays regard to every circumstance in that with which it has to deal" (cf. Tr., Syn., § x).†

G1168.def:
δειλιάω, -ῶ
(δειλία), [in LXX for חתת ni., פּחד, etc. ;] 
= the more frequently ἀποδ-, to be cowardly, timid, fearful: Jean 14:27.†

G1169.def:
δειλός, -ή, όν 
(δέος), [in LXX for רַךְ, etc. ;] 
cowardly, fearful: Matthieu 8:26, Marc 4:40, Apocalypse 21:8.†

G1170.def:
δεῖνα, ὁ, ἡ, τό (genitive -νος, dative -νι, accusative -να), 
[in Aq.: Ruth 4:1, 1 Rois 21:2 (3) (Sm. also), 4Ki.6:8 * ;] 
such an one, a certain one, whom one cannot or will not name: Matthieu 26:18.†

G1171.def:
δεινῶς , 
adv. (δέος), [in LXX: Job 10:16, Wis.17:3, al. ;] 
__1. terribly: Matthieu 8:6. 
__2. vehemently: Luc 11:53.†

G1172.def:
δειπνέω, -ῶ 
(δεῖπνον, which see), [in LXX: Proverbes 23:1 (לחם), Tob.7:8 8:1, Dan LXX 11:27 * ;] 
to take the chief meal of the day, to dine, to sup: Luc 17:8 22:20 (WH, br., R, mg. omits), 1 Corinthiens 11:25; metaphorically, Apocalypse 3:20.†

G1173.def:
δεῖπνον, -ου, τό 
[in LXX chiefly for פַּת־בַּג (Da) ;] 
the chief meal of the day, dinner, supper: Matthieu 23:6, Marc 12:39, Luc 14:17, 24 20:46, Jean 13:2, 4 21:20, 1 Corinthiens 11:21; δ. ποιεῖν, Marc 6:21, Luc 14:12, 16, Jean 12:2; κυριακὸν (which see) δ., 1 Corinthiens 11:20; metaphorically (Dalman, Words, 118), δ. τ. γάμου τ. ἀρνίου, Apocalypse 19:9; δ. τ. μέγα τ. Θεοῦ, Apocalypse 19:17.†

G1174.def:
δεισι-δαίμων, -ον
(δείδω, to fear; δαίμων, deity) 
reverent to the deity, religious; compar. -μονεστέρους (AV, too superstitious, R, txt., somewhat superstitious, a sense in wh. the word is sometimes used; cf. Field, Notes, 125), more religious, God fearing, than others, quite religious (Abbott, Essays, 105 ff.; Deiss., LAE, 285): Actes 17:22.† 
SYN.: εὐσεβής (which see), θεοσεβής, θρῆσκος (Cremer, 681; DB, ext., 142 a).

G1176.def:
δέκα, οἱ, αἱ, τά, 
ten: Matthieu 20:24, al.; θλίψις ἡμερῶν δ., i.e. of brief duration: Apocalypse 2:10.†
δεκα-οκτώ, T for δέκα ὀκτώ, 
eighteen: Luc 13:4.†

G1178.def:
δεκα-πέντε 
[in LXX: Exode 27:15, 1Ma.10:40, al. ;] 
late form of πεντεκαίδεκα, fifteen: Jean 11:18, Actes 27:5, WH, mg., ib. 28, Galates 1:18.†

G1179.def:
Δεκά-πολις, -εως, ὴ 
Decapolis, a region east of the Jordan con­taining ten cities: Matthieu 4:25, Marc 5:20 7:31.†

G1180.def:
δεκατέσσαρες, -ων, oἱ, αἱ, -α, τά 
[in LXX: Genèse 31:41, Tob.8:19, al. ;] 
= cl. τεσσαρεσκαίδεκα, more frequently in later Gk. than the older form and in MGr. (for thirteen and upwards) universal, fourteen: Matthieu 1:17, 2 Corinthiens 12:2, Galates 2:1 (cf. τεσσαρεσκαιδέκατος).†

G1182.def:
δέκατος, -η, -ον 
(δέκα), [in LXX for מַעֲשֵׂר and cognate forms ;] 
tenth: Jean 1:40, Actes 19:9 (WH, txt., RV omit), Apocalypse 11:13; 21:20.†

G1183.def:
δεκατόω, -ῶ, 
= cl. -τεύω (δεκάτη), [in LXX: Néhémie 10:37 (38) (עשׂר pi.) * ;] 
to take tithe of: with accusative of person(s), Hébreux 7:6; pass. to pay tithe: Hébreux 7:9.†

G1184.def:
δεκτός, -ή, -όν 
verbal adj. of δέχομαι, [in LXX chiefly for רָצוֹן: Proverbes 11:1, al. ;] 
acceptable: Luc 4:19 (LXX) 24, Actes 10:35, 2 Corinthiens 6:2" (LXX), Philippiens 4:18 (cf. εὐπροσδ-).†

G1185.def:
δελεάζω
(δέλεαρ, a bait), 
to allure by a bait: metaphorically, to allure, entice: with accusative, 2 Pierre 2:14, 18; pass., Jacques 1:14.†

G1186.def:
δένδρον, -ου, τό
[in LXX for עֵץ, etc. ;] 
a tree: Matthieu 3:10, al.; δ. ἀγαθόν, Matthieu 7:17, 18; δ. καλόν, Matthieu 12:33, Luc 6:43; δ. σαπρόν, Matthieu 7:17, 18 12:33, Luc 6:43; γίνεσθαι δ., Matthieu 13:32; γ. εἰς δ., Luc 13:19.

G1187.def:
δεξιολάβος, -ου, ὁ 
(δεξιός, λαμβάνω), 
a kind of soldier, prob. a spearman (Vg., lancearius) or slinger: Actes 23:23.†
δεξιο-βόλος, -ου, ὁ
(δεξιός, βάλλω), 
one who throws with the right hand: L for δεξιολάβος, Actes 23:23.†

G1188.def:
δεξιός, -ά, -όν 
[in LXX chiefly for יָמִין ;] 
the right: Matthieu 5:29, Jean 18:10, al.; ὅπλα δ., weapons carried in the right hand, i.e. for offence, 2 Corinthiens 6:7 ; ἡ δ. χείρ, Matthieu 5:30, Luc 6:6, al.; ἡ δ. (sc. χείρ), Matthieu 6:3, al.; ἐπὶ τὴν δ., in the right hand (R, txt., on R, mg.), Apocalypse 5:1; διδόναι τὴν δ., in friend­ship (Deiss., BS, 251), Galates 2:9; metaphorically of power, τῇ δ. αὐτοῦ, Actes 2:33 5:31; τὰ δ., the right side, Marc 16:5; ἐκ δεξιῶν, on the right hand, with genitive, Matthieu 25:33, 34, Marc 15:27, Luc 1:11, al.; of a place of honour in the Messianic Kingdom (cf. 3Ki.2:19, Psa.44(45):10), καθίσαι ἐκ δεξιῶν, Matthieu 20:21, Marc 10:37; of the heavenly session of Christ, Matthieu 26:64, Marc 14:62, Hébreux 1:13 (Cremer, 172)

G1191.def:
Δέρβη, -ης, ἡ, 
Derbe, a city of Lycaonia: Actes 14:6, 20 16:1.†

G1192.def:
δέρμα, -τος, τό
(δέρω), [in LXX for עוֹר ;] 
the skin, hide of beasts: ἐν αἰγίοις δ., Hébreux 11:37.†

G1193.def:
δερμάτινος, -η, -ον
(δέρμα), [in LXX for עוֹר ;] 
of skin, leathern: Matthieu 3:4, Marc 1:6 (cf. 4Ki.1:8).†

G1194.def:
δέρω 
[in LXX: Lévitique 1:6, 2 Chroniques 29:34; 35:11 (פָּשַׁט hi.)* ;] 
__1. to skin, flay. 
__2. (of. Eng. slang, hide) to beat, thrash: with accusative, Matthieu 21:35, Marc 12:3, 5, Luc 20:10, 11 22:63, Jean 18:23, Actes 5:40 16:37 22:19; ὡς ἀέρα δέρων, 1 Corinthiens 9:26; εἰς πρόσωπου δ., 2 Corinthiens 11:20. Pass., Marc 13:9, Luc 12:47, 48 (δαρήσεται πολλάς, ὀλίγας, Sc. πληγάς).†

G1195.def:
δεσμεύω
(δεσμός), [in LXX for אָסַר (Juges 16:11, al.), אָלַם pi. (Genèse 37:7, al.), etc. ;] 
__1. to put in chains: Luc 8:29, Actes 22:4. 
__2. to bind, tie together: φορτία, Matthieu 23:4.†

G1197.def:
δέσμη (Rec. δεσμή), -ης, ἡ 
(δέω), [in LXX for אֲגֻדָּה, Exode 12:22 * ;] 
a bundle: δήσατε αὐτὰ εἰς δέσμας (D, Orig., omit εἰς, and Blass thinks original reading, δέσμας δέσμας; see Deiss., LAE, 125.4), Matthieu 13:30.†

G1198.def:
δέσμιος, -ον (also -α, -ον; 
δεσμός), [in LXX for אסר;] 
__1. binding. 
__2. bound, captive; ὁ δ., as subst., a prisoner: Matthieu 27:15, 16, Marc 15:6, Actes 16:25, 27 23:18 25:14, 27 28:16 (Rec.) 17, Hébreux 10:34 13:3; ὁ δ. τοῦ Χριστοῦ, Éphésiens 3:1, 2 Timothée 1:8, Phm 1, 9; ὁ δ. ἐν κυρίῳ, Éphésiens 4:1.†

G1199.def:
δεσμός, -οῦ, ὁ
(δέω), [in LXX chiefly for אסר ;] 
a band, bond: metaphorically, Luc 13:16; ὁ δεσμὸς τ. γλώσσης, Marc 7:35 (for this expression in π., see Deiss., LAE, 306 ff.; of actual bonds, see Ruth., Gr., 9). Pl., δεσμοί, Philippiens 1:13; δεσμά (as also in cl.), Luc 8:29, Actes 16:26 20:23; genitive, dative, Actes 23:29 26:29, 31, Philippiens 1:7, 14, 17, Colossiens 4:18, 2 Timothée 2:9, Phm 10, Hébreux 11:36, Ju 6; ἐν τοῖς δ. τοῦ εὐαγγελίου Phm 13.†
